title: Trajectory Functionals in the Thermodynamics of Radiation-Induced Damage in Structural Materials
abstract: This paper delivers a novel self-consistent non-local kinetic framework based on dose-dependent semi-Markov renewal transport and the generalized Doob's h-transform to evaluate the structural degradation of WWER-1000/1200 fuel claddings. By leveraging the Feynman-Kac formalism, we map the continuous microscopic defect path trajectories generated by the Liouville operator directly onto the evolution of the macroscopically integrated damage potential. The framework accounts for long-range memory effects in the degradation kinetics via a non-vanishing structural commutator of the path Liouville operator and Zwanzig-Mori projection operators, which mathematically links the spatial restrictions of microscopic sinks to energetic path penalties. Spatial profiling of the cladding's mean lifetime, demonstrates a distinct sigmoidal, S-shaped degradation trajectory encompassing distinct incubation, linear growth, and avalanche breakdown stages. The numerical results reveal an abrupt, localized reduction in the operational lifespan near the cladding boundaries. This marginal vulnerability is shown to be a direct physical consequence of boundary stress field singularities at the fuel cladding interface and localized embrittlement. The developed path integral architecture provides a strict thermodynamic link between non-equilibrium fluctuations and the global Griffiths macro-barrier, offering a robust predictive tool for high-burnup nuclear fuel safety assessments.
summary: This theoretical paper develops a sophisticated kinetic framework to model radiation-induced structural degradation in nuclear materials. It maps complex, stochastic defect trajectories onto a macroscopic damage potential using advanced tools from non-equilibrium statistical mechanics. The resulting model successfully predicts the characteristic S-shaped failure curve and highlights critical boundary vulnerabilities.
main_problem: The paper addresses the structural degradation of materials due to radiation damage by linking microscopic defect path dynamics to macroscopic damage potential.
main_result: The analysis predicts a characteristic sigmoidal, S-shaped degradation trajectory, showing an abrupt, localized reduction in operational lifespan near material boundaries.
method: It employs a novel non-local kinetic framework utilizing the Feynman-Kac formalism, generalized Doob's h-transform, and semi-Markov renewal transport theory.
model_or_system: The system modeled is WWER-1000/1200 fuel claddings subjected to intense neutron irradiation, treated via a two-level hierarchical description.
key_observables: The integrated damage potential ($\Phi$), the conditional survival probability ($h(x, t)$), and the mean lifetime ($	au_{	ext{avg}}$).
important_parameters: Radiation dose (dpa), structural commutator terms, and the critical absorbing macro-barrier ($x_c$).
main_assumptions: The approach assumes the failure of classical models to capture non-linear stochasticity and relies on the mathematical closure provided by the generalized Zubarev nonequilibrium statistical operator.
figures_summary: Figures illustrate the spatial-temporal evolution of the survival probability $h(x, t)$ across different degradation stages and plot the macroscopic damage potential $\Phi_j$ exhibiting the characteristic S-shaped curve.
paper_structure: The paper develops a framework by first establishing the stochastic process, then deriving the non-local semi-Markov transport operator (adjoint Doob equation), and finally applying this to model the three distinct stages of material failure kinetics.
why_interesting: The rigorous application of path integrals and non-equilibrium statistical mechanics (like the Doob transform) to model irreversible, history-dependent degradation processes provides advanced tools applicable to open quantum systems far from equilibrium.
